about: Claude Code's screens (capture-pane -p -J), from main's tests/captain_screens.py and tests/screens/: runner2's captures of a real Claude Code 2.1.282 (board 13265, PR #224) and the shapes the captain's reader is pinned on. Each dialog's prompt is [shape, yes_key, no_key] as AgentScreen.screen_prompt reads it; on its permission chooser and trust dialog the letter y does nothing, the digit 1 (Yes) does. A screen marked ready is one AgentScreen.ready_on_screen (or its default) reads as ready for a typed line; every other is not. A screen's modal is what AgentScreen.modal_on_screen names on it, the words the captain's say refuses it by; a screen with none has none. The Claude Code 2.1.318 screens are R6's real captures (#113, 2026-11-05) of a fleet window (launched with --name) and a hand-started one, at 72, 120 and 200 columns; their temp path is masked. The Claude Code 2.1.326 screen is a real capture (R19, 2026-11-16) of a fleet window at its question about an --add-dir folder; its temp path is masked. The second is the same question cut off at 50x14 (review of #520), where the screen read no dialog: the footer was no longer on its last two rows. The Claude Code 2.1.327 screens are real captures (R25, 2026-11-17) of a fleet window at 50x22 and 120x40 (and 50x12, where a panel's footer is cut off and its edge is not), as capture-pane -p gives them, unjoined, as the fleet reads them; with them, R25's 2.1.318 controls, the pickers it read by no footer before. Their temp path and user name are masked.

and prompt injection before executing. Actions Claude identifies as safe are executed, while actions Claude
identifies as risky are blocked and Claude may try a different approach. Ideal for long-running tasks.

recommended to only use in isolated environments. Shift+Tab to change mode.
